audit.why: Packet levelChart is [Quinn, Quinn, Quinn, Skill, Skill, Skill, Teemo] and matches the whys once rows 0, 5 and 6 are corrected. The 49.74% win rate over 575 games fits a lane that starts Quinn-favoured and ends Teemo-favoured.
audit.corrected: Row 0 to Quinn, row 5 to Skill, row 6 to Teemo, proposed as one atomic group across both layers, with phases[6].why rewritten to match.

audit.why: Quinn levels 1-3, her own W at level 2, level 6 as a roam rather than a duel, Teemo late with shrooms — right and ordered, and spikes[2] correctly refuses to sell Behind Enemy Lines as duel power. Blinding Dart's flat 7s and Move Quick's 14s now attached.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The best interaction in this matchup is absent from every field: Heightened Senses (W) reveals a 2100-unit area and answers stealth, which strips Guerrilla Warfare — the invisibility that lets Teemo open trades from brush. Two supporting facts were also missing: Blinding Dart is 680 range against Quinn's 1025-range Blinding Assault, so she pokes from outside it; and blinding Teemo back denies Toxic Shot, because the poison is applied on-hit by his basic attacks.
audit.why: Riot text for Teemo's passive: 'If he's in brush, Teemo can enter and maintain his Invisibility while moving.' Quinn's W carries revealsStealth ('answers stealth champions') at 2100 range. Riot text for Toxic Shot: 'Each of Teemo's attacks will poison the target On-Hit' — a basic-attack effect, so a blind stops it.
audit.corrected: Reveal-vs-invisibility written into report[5].t and wants.you[1]; the range advantage and the Toxic Shot consequence written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blinding Dart was described without its cooldown, and the page tells the player to 'trade around Blinding Dart's cooldown' with no number.
audit.why: It is a flat 7 seconds at every rank — unusually, it never gets shorter, which makes the punish window identical all game and worth stating once.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] warned about chasing through shrooms without saying what they do, and the kit file's knockup flag on Noxious Trap is a false positive.
audit.why: The mirror audit confirms this: mushrooms slow and damage over time, they do not displace. The flag appears to derive from the word 'bounce' in Riot's description of a mushroom thrown onto another mushroom.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now states slow and poison and nothing else, so the derived flag never reaches the page.

notes: Teemo's move speed is Move Quick (W); the page had it on his passive, which is Guerrilla Warfare (invisibility). Fixing that also surfaced the matchup's best unrecorded interaction — Quinn's Heightened Senses hard-counters his brush invisibility — which now appears in two places. Carrying forward the mirror's warning: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json carries a false 'knockup' flag on Noxious Trap, and that false positive has propagated into _missing-interactions.json, so any agent trusting the flag will write a displacement that does not exist. I kept it off this page.
